subject: Media Studies

outcomes.text: Explain how media forms, codes, conventions and techniques communicate meanings.
Understand how codes and conventions develop media language as genre.
Explain the importance of challenging or subverting media conventions.
Analyse how media language incorporates viewpoints and ideologies.
Explain how audiences respond to and interpret media language.
Understand how technological developments affect media language.
Analyse how combinations of media language create meaning.
Understand that genre is dynamic and changes historically.
Explain how selection and combination represent events, issues, individuals and social groups.
Understand how representation mediates particular versions of reality.
Explain why producers choose particular ways to represent people, events and issues.
Analyse how social and cultural contexts influence representations.
Explain why groups may be under-represented or misrepresented nationally and globally.
Analyse how representations communicate and reinforce values, attitudes and beliefs.
Explain how audiences interpret and respond to media representations.
Understand how historical context affects representations.
Analyse how representations invoke discourses and ideologies and position audiences.
Explain how interpretations of representation reflect social, cultural and historical circumstances.
Explain how production, distribution and consumption processes shape media products.
Understand production, distribution and consumption by organisations, groups and individuals globally.
Understand the specialised and institutional nature of media production, distribution and consumption.
Explain relationships between technological change and media production, distribution and consumption.
Understand ownership and control, including conglomerates, vertical integration and diversification.
Explain how economic factors and funding models affect media industries and products.
Explain how media organisations maintain varied local, national and global audiences, including through marketing.
Understand contemporary media regulation and technological change's effects on it.
Explain how convergent platforms affect media production, distribution and consumption.
Discuss production, distribution, marketing, audience consumption and relationships between audiences and institutions.
Understand how ownership and funding affect contemporary media practice.
Explain the importance of cross-media convergence and synergy in production, distribution and marketing.
Understand technologies introduced recently across production, distribution, marketing and consumption.
Explain how technological developments affect institutions and audiences.
Understand the importance of technological convergence for institutions and audiences.
Explain how industries group audiences by demographics, lifestyle and taste.
Explain how producers target, attract, reach, address and construct audiences.
Understand how content, appeal, marketing, distribution and consumption target audiences.
Explain relationships between media technologies and patterns of consumption and response.
Analyse how audiences interpret texts differently using theories and ideologies.
Understand how audiences interact with media and participate in production.
Explain how specialised audiences are reached locally, nationally and globally through technologies and platforms.
Understand how organisations address mass and specialised audience needs through targeting.
Explain how demographic, identity and cultural factors shape media use.
Understand the importance of niche and fan audiences to media.
Analyse issues in targeting national and local audiences by global institutions.
Relate personal media consumption to wider audience behaviour patterns and trends.
Analyse how moving-image technical language and conventions create meaning for audiences.
Explain how technical elements create representations and communicate socially significant messages and values.
Use camera shots, angles, movement and composition to analyse meaning.
Analyse how sound, including dialogue, effects, music and voiceover, creates meaning.
Analyse how mise-en-scène, including setting, costume, props, lighting and colour, creates meaning.
Analyse how editing, transitions, continuity and visual effects create meaning.
Study studios or production companies, including film production, distribution, exhibition and audience consumption.
Study contemporary digital and physical film distribution and its effects on production, marketing and consumption.
Study record labels and independent producers, including music production, distribution, marketing and audience consumption.
Understand wider issues surrounding digital music distribution.
Study contemporary newspaper or magazine publishing and its production, distribution and consumption.
Understand how technological change challenges and reshapes print publishing.
Understand contemporary and historical approaches to regulating media.
Evaluate arguments supporting and opposing particular forms of media regulation.
Assess how effectively regulatory practices impose or recommend sanctions.
Understand wider social issues associated with media regulation.
Explain how different regulatory bodies address ownership, morality and accuracy.
Understand the legal and ethical frameworks governing media producers and distributors.
Analyse relationships among media texts, producers, distributors and audiences.
Analyse how national, regional, individual and group identities are mediated.
Understand the changing power relationships within and between audiences and the media.
Understand how rhetoric creates power in media.
Analyse how campaigning and marketing messages are constructed and received.
Understand how media access can be restricted, controlled or democratically distributed.
Understand how audiences engage with evolving media environments.
Understand convergence between personal communication and mass communication technologies.
Assess how technological change affects society, including information sharing and data protection.
Understand globalisation and how audiences and institutions respond to it.
Analyse changing media ownership and distribution models, including net neutrality.
Analyse representations of public and private personae.
Understand relationships among software, hardware and audiences.
Assess how developing technologies influence media language.
Understand changing reception modes and their effects on audiences.
Distinguish historical, stylistic and theoretical versions of postmodernism.
Evaluate arguments about whether particular media forms should be considered postmodern.
Analyse how postmodern texts can alter traditional relationships between texts and audiences.
Understand the relationship between postmodernism and popular culture.
Explain how audiences and media industries may operate differently in a postmodern world.
Understand the relationship between postmodernism and narrative.
